Theme

wave noun

also billow, surge, breaker

classical

unda, undae f.

noun, first declension

Other words

  • flūctus, flūctūs m. — a wave, a billow, above all of the sea

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 9.16.6: flūctum ā saxō frangī (Lewis & Short); Cic. Fin. 5.5: ad flūctum ajunt dēclāmāre solitum Dēmosthenem (Lewis & Short)

    From fluō; most often in the plural.

Examples

  • Ecce unda magna.

    Here comes a big wave.composed

  • Vīs undās magnās an parvās?

    Do you want big waves or little waves?composed

  • Undās fac.

    Make waves.composed

  • ad flūctum ajunt dēclāmāre solitum Dēmosthenem, ut fremitum assuēsceret vōce vincere

    they say Demosthenes used to declaim to the waves, to accustom himself to mastering a roar with his voiceCic. Fin. 5.5 (Lewis & Short)

See also sea, billow, Sailor and Waves, a storm in a teacup.

SourcesLewis & Short: unda

Lewis & Short: fluctus
